answer: At dawn, a new agent cannot simply join the grove of trusted traders and harvest rewards. Each identity must stake a refundable bond and build a verifiable history of useful work, like tending a garden over weeks: completed tasks, peer attestations, and consistent behavior accumulate slowly. Creating a thousand fake identities would require a thousand bonds and a thousand histories, so the cost of a sybil flood rises linearly while honest agents pay only once. Misbehavior slashes the bond, making fake identities expensive to create and worthless to burn.
